subject: On-prem validation: KV-cache warmup & sanity handoff
messages:
From: Tara Patel <tara@acme-tech.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem go-live: validation checklist & KV-cache warmup plan

Hi team,

We're finalizing the on-prem cutover plan for Acme's VPC deployment next week and want to align on the KV-cache warmup + smoke sequence so we don't hit cold-start slowness post-cutover. Attached is our suggested runbook draft (runbook_onprem_v1.pdf). Key asks: 

- Confirm the warmup order: networking (BGP/ACLs) -> service health -> KV-cache bulk-populate -> small-scale traffic ramp.
- Approve the smoke tests: L4 connectivity sweep, TLS handshake verification, 3 healthcheck endpoints (liveness, readiness, kv-ttl), sample inference path (100 short requests), and graceful-fallback test to hosted variant.
- Share on-call rotation for the 2-hour cutover window (UTC time in runbook).

We expect the warmup to take ~35 minutes total; the bulk-populate step will be split across 4 workers to avoid backend spikes.

Attachments: runbook_onprem_v1.pdf (draft), connectivity-diagram.png (network view).

Can you confirm by EOD Friday so we can freeze the runbook?

Thanks,
Tara
Tara Patel
Head of Platform, Acme Tech
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Tara Patel <tara@acme-tech.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem go-live: validation checklist & KV-cache warmup plan

Tara — thanks, this is a good starting point. A couple of quick notes from the runtime side: 

- Order: I agree with network -> service -> cache. One tweak: run a lightweight readiness sweep after service health but before bulk-populate; any 5xxs at that point should abort the warmup and revert routing.
- KV warmup: we'll prime keys in sequence: namespace metadata first, then model weights metadata, then recent sessions. Bulk-populate size per worker should be capped at 250 req/s to avoid stampeding the storage tier.
- Smoke tests: add a KV TTL validation (write/read a sentinel key and verify TTL reduction after 30s).

On-call: Priyom will lead infra during the window; Soojin handles networking ACLs and route validation; Marissa will run the customer-facing smoke (inference path and correctness checks).

I've uploaded a short healthcheck sample to the internal drive: https://drive.company.com/drive/folders/1a2B-onprem-runbooks and created JIRA-OPS-4821 for pre-cutover tasks.

Quick curl for the health endpoint we like to use for readiness: 

  curl -sS -X GET "https://10.4.2.11:8443/healthz?check=readiness" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -k 

If anyone objects to the rate cap or ordering, speak now — otherwise we'll freeze the sequence and run a rehearsal on Monday.

michael
Michael Grant
Director, Inference Ops — Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Tara Patel <tara@acme-tech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem go-live: validation checklist & KV-cache warmup plan

All — ran the rehearsal this morning against the staging cluster and attached the smoke scripts and a trimmed connectivity diagram for reference. Observations: 

- L4 sweep passed across all subnets; a stale ACL entry in subnet-3 caused a short fail during the first pass but was cleared by Soojin and re-tested.
- Service health endpoints returned 200 within expected bounds once the DB sidecars finished init (approx +18s).
- KV warmup: our 4 workers completed the namespace metadata pass and model metadata pass without exceeding the 250 req/s cap. We throttled the session keys slightly to avoid storage GC spikes.
- Rehearsal inference path: 95/100 requests returned under 120ms; 5 were 503s during an ephemeral spike but auto-fallback to hosted model completed and requests returned within the SLA window.

Attachments: smoke_scripts.sh, connectivity-diagram.png (trimmed).

Plan for cutover: begin the run at 07:00 UTC on Wednesday, perform a canary at +10min, then full traffic at +40min if canary is clean. I'll be on-call for infra.

Cheers,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Staff Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: On-prem go-live: validation checklist & KV-cache warmup plan

FYI — Atlas Cloud was on-site for the rehearsal and we collected the smoke logs. Summary: 

- Canary (10% traffic) went green after KV warmup. Warmup completed in 28 minutes total with the 4-worker configuration.
- Observed 12 transient 503s during the first 10 minutes of canary (same spike Priyom saw), but the routing fallback to hosted model triggered and there was no customer-visible error.
- Post-warmup latency baseline averaged 110ms p50 for the short inference path (within SLAs).
- Actions before full traffic: extend the KV sentinel TTL test to 60s in the runbook and add a 2-minute wait window between canary confirmation and ramp to full traffic to surface delayed failures.

I've attached the raw logs: smoke_logs_20270614.zip. If the team is comfortable with the extra wait and TTL tweak, consider this green for final signoff from Atlas.

Next steps: Michael / Priyom — if you confirm the TTL/hold changes I'll update the runbook and we can proceed with the planned Wednesday cutover.

—Leo
Leo Morris
Partner Solutions Engineer — Atlas Cloud
